primitives.name: Closed Market Hypothesis
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The NFL game market is closed.** ~190 specifications tested out of sample.
primitives.assumptions: All public information is priced into the market. No exploitable inefficiency remains in side or total bets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Out-of-sample testing reveals no persistent alpha across 190 specifications.

layer2.mapping: Market efficiency implies that any model-derived edge is either non-existent or ephemeral. The closed market hypothesis maps to a degenerate optimization problem where model skill cannot be sustained.
layer2.telemetry: Holdout Brier score of model vs market (0.251 vs 0.220)

primitives.name: Orthogonal Signal Calibration
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Our engine has negative standalone skill and a real orthogonal signal.** Head-to-head on 540 identical picks: model Brier 0.251, market 0.220, a constant 0.248.
primitives.assumptions: Model and market are independent; model provides orthogonal information that improves calibration when combined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model skill is negative, blending with market improves calibration via shrinkage.

layer2.mapping: Calibration gain from shrinkage operation p = market + 0.10·(model - market) reflects a derived kernel of signal orthogonality and marginal utility.
layer2.telemetry: Holdout Brier score improves from 0.251 to 0.20818

primitives.name: Shrinkage Calibration Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: **At 10% weight blended toward the market it beats the market out of sample** (0.20818 vs 0.20905; football 0.18825 vs 0.18946).
primitives.assumptions: The model's error is unbiased but noisy; shrinkage reduces variance without biasing toward market.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When model skill is low, shrinkage toward market improves calibration and reduces overconfidence.

layer2.mapping: Operator defines a linear transformation from raw model output to calibrated estimate. Maps to a Bayesian posterior update under weak prior assumption.
layer2.telemetry: Improved Brier score on holdout set (0.20818 vs 0.20905)

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that the NFL market is closed, meaning no exploitable inefficiency remains in public data. This implies that any model attempting to predict outcomes must rely on orthogonal signals rather than direct predictive skill. The engine's standalone performance is poor (Brier 0.251), but its orthogonal signal allows for calibration gains when blended with the market (Brier 0.20818). The shrinkage operator p = market + 0.10·(model - market) represents a minimal adjustment that improves calibration without introducing new edge. This is a dualistic system: the model is a noisy proxy, and the market is the baseline. The failure mode occurs if the model becomes too confident or if the orthogonal signal degrades. The system must remain calibrated and avoid overfitting to past performance.
